draft.title: The war against Japan
card: Japan took Manchuria in 1931. In 1937 it launched a full invasion of China. The Nationalist government under Jiang Jieshi and the Communists faced a common enemy.
Japan's forces took the major coastal cities and richest farmland. The Nationalists lost their main sources of tax and industry and moved their capital inland to Chongqing.
The Nationalist army fought large battles and suffered heavy losses. Its government also faced inflation and corruption, and it lost public support.

The Communists, based in the north-west, used guerrilla warfare behind Japanese lines. They won peasant support by resisting Japan and by reducing rents in the areas they held. Their army and party grew much larger.
draft.remember: The war drained the Nationalists and gave the Communists room to grow among peasants.

a.q: Why did the war against Japan weaken the Nationalist government?
opts: It lost rich cities and taxes, and its army took heavy losses
It had to give up its army so that the Communists could lead
It lost peasant support because it chose to end the war early
It was forced to move its capital to the Communist base area
a.why: The Nationalists lost the coastal cities and farmland that funded them, and their army suffered heavy losses in large battles. They did not give up their army, and they did not end the war early. Their capital moved to Chongqing, not to the Communist base.
a.clue: Think about what the Nationalists lost and what their army faced.

b.q: A village in northern China in 1940 lies behind Japanese lines. Its farmers begin to back the Communists. What is the most likely reason?
opts: The Communists resisted Japan and reduced the farmers' rents
The Nationalists had taken the village's land to fund the war
The farmers had already read Marxist books on class struggle
The Communists had won the cities and sent food to the village
b.why: The card says the Communists won peasant support by resisting Japan and reducing rents in the areas they held. The Communists did not hold the cities then, and the card does not say the farmers were drawn by Marxist reading or by Nationalist land seizures.
b.clue: Look at what the Communists did in the areas they held.
